title: User Guide
subtitle: A little guidance. A lot more clarity.
description: Learn to organize your everyday work, one step at a time.
independent: Separate workspace on each device, browser profile and site address.
futureDiagram: Optional account → cloud sync → your devices. Local work and offline access remain part of the vision.

helpDescription: Learn to use your workspace, install the app and keep a backup.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.intro: Everything in its orbit. A calm place for projects and everyday plans.

sections.title: Your work, at your pace
paragraphs: Saturnino helps you break a goal into small tasks and see what comes next. Use it for studies, freelance work, personal projects or everyday activities. No account is required.

sections.title: Meet your workspace
paragraphs: <label>Overview</label> shows progress. <label>My Tasks</label> combines tasks from all projects. <label>Projects</label> opens each project's list or board. <label>Settings</label> holds appearance, sidebar, local workspace information, backups and help. The header's <action>Go back</action> button returns through known workspace pages, with a safe <label>Overview</label> fallback.

sections.title: One example throughout
paragraphs: <example>Website redesign</example> is our fictional project. We will plan <example>Create wireframes</example> and move it from <status value="todo">To do</status> to <status value="done">Done</status>. Screenshots use demonstration data only. They show the English interface; translated captions explain each action and your own interface follows your selected language.

quick-start.title: Quick Start
quick-start.intro: Create a project, plan a task and review progress.

sections.title: Open and create
steps: Open Saturnino. Choose <label>Projects</label> in the sidebar; on a small screen, open the navigation menu first.
Choose <action>New project</action>. In <label>Project name</label>, enter <example>Website redesign</example>.
Add a <label>Description</label> and choose a <label>Project color</label>. Select <action>Create project</action>.
Choose <action>View project</action> to open your new project.

sections.title: Add and plan
steps: Inside the project, choose <action>New task</action>.
In <label>Task title</label>, enter <example>Create wireframes</example>. Add a <label>Description</label> if useful.
Set <label>Priority</label> to <priority value="high">High</priority> and <label>Status</label> to <status value="todo">To do</status>. Choose a realistic <label>Due date</label>.
Select <action>Create task</action> to save.

sections.title: Organize and review
steps: Choose <label>Board</label> inside the project.
Move <example>Create wireframes</example> to <status value="in-progress">In progress</status> when you start and <status value="done">Done</status> when finished. Drag the card or use its task menu.
Open <label>Overview</label> to review progress and choose your next step.

installation.title: Installation
installation.intro: Keep Saturnino close, without an App Store or Google Play download.

sections.title: Before you install
paragraphs: Open Saturnino online in a compatible browser. Installation and offline readiness are different: check <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Local Workspace</label></path> and wait for the message: <label>Ready for offline use.</label> Browser menus and availability vary by version.

sections.title: Choose your device
paragraphs: Follow the platform instructions below. The optional install button appears only when this browser supplies an installation request. A missing button does not stop you using a normal browser tab.

sections.title: Check your local workspace
paragraphs: Do not assume installing, switching browsers or opening a standalone web app copies existing data. Export JSON first and check the destination. Use the same browser profile and address, or restore manually when needed.
sections.note: Installation does not transfer data between browsers or devices. Export a JSON backup before moving your workspace.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Give every goal its own space.

sections.title: Create and open
steps: <path><label>Projects</label> → <action>New project</action></path>: enter <label>Project name</label> (up to 80 characters), an optional <label>Description</label> (up to 500) and <label>Project color</label>.
Choose <action>Create project</action>, then <action>View project</action>. Separate work, studies and personal goals into recognizable projects.

sections.title: Favorites and quick access
paragraphs: Use a project's star to add or remove it from <label>Favorites</label>. <label>Recent Projects</label> follows your visits. <label>Project Explorer</label> searches project names and opens them from the sidebar; its plus button creates a project. Open the navigation menu first on mobile.

sections.title: Edit or delete thoughtfully
steps: Open the project actions menu and select <action>Edit project</action>. Update <label>Project name</label>, <label>Description</label>, <label>Project color</label> and select <action>Save changes</action>.
<action>Delete project</action> requires confirmation and permanently removes the project AND all related tasks.
There is no undo or trash.
Export a backup before deleting anything you may need.
sections.warning: <action>Delete project</action> permanently removes the project and all its tasks. There is no undo. Download a JSON backup before confirming.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.intro: Turn a plan into a concrete action.

sections.title: Add the essentials
steps: Choose <action>New task</action> from a project or <label>My Tasks</label>.
Enter a <label>Task title</label> (up to 120 characters) and select an existing <label>Project</label>.
Add an optional <label>Description</label> (up to 2,000 characters).

Choose <label>Status</label>, <label>Priority</label> and an optional <label>Due date</label> in the calendar. Priorities are <priority value="low">Low</priority>, <priority value="medium">Medium</priority>, <priority value="high">High</priority> and <priority value="urgent">Urgent</priority>.
Select <action>Create task</action> to save.

sections.title: Open, edit and delete
steps: A simple title click opens details: a side panel on desktop or full-screen panel on mobile.
Change fields and choose <action>Save task</action>.
<action>Cancel</action> leaves changes unsaved; a dirty form asks whether to continue or discard.
A conflict message protects against another tab's edit.
<action>Delete task</action> requires confirmation and is permanent.
sections.warning: <action>Delete task</action> is permanent. Keep a JSON backup if you may need this task again.

sections.title: Search, filter and change views
steps: Use <label>Search tasks</label> to find titles and descriptions.
Open <label>Filters</label> and combine <label>Filter by status</label>, <label>Filter by priority</label>, <label>Filter by project</label>, <label>Filter by due date</label>.
Remove individual chips or <action>Clear filters</action>.

Use <label>Sort tasks</label> to choose <label>Manual order</label>, <label>Due date, soonest first</label>, <label>Priority, highest first</label>, <label>Title, A–Z</label> or <label>Recently updated</label>.
<label>Projects</label> offer <label>List</label> or <label>Board</label>; <label>My Tasks</label> is a cross-project list.
Filters or nonmanual sorting restrict reordering so hidden tasks do not lead to misleading positions.

kanban.title: Kanban Board
kanban.intro: See work move from idea to completion.

sections.title: Four clear stages
bullets: <status value="backlog">Backlog</status>: ideas and future tasks you are not starting yet.
<status value="todo">To do</status>: tasks ready to begin.
<status value="in-progress">In progress</status>: work you are actively doing.
<status value="done">Done</status>: finished tasks; project progress updates automatically.

sections.title: Drag and reorder
steps: With a mouse, press a title or noninteractive surface and move enough to activate drag.
A simple title click still opens details.
The card changes appearance, the destination column is outlined and a line shows insertion before a target task or at the end.
Release to save status and order; both survive reload.
Move <example>Create wireframes</example> from <status value="todo">To do</status> to <status value="in-progress">In progress</status> when starting.

sections.title: Keyboard and touch alternatives
steps: Focus the drag handle with <key>Tab</key>. Press <key>Space</key> or <key>Enter</key> to pick up the task, use the arrow keys to move, and press <key>Space</key> or <key>Enter</key> to drop. Press <key>Escape</key> to cancel.
Or open the task menu and use <label>Move to</label> to choose a status. Its move up and move down actions reorder the task.
Menus work well on touch screens.
Touch dragging needs a short hold; quick scroll gestures remain scrolling.
Scroll horizontally to reach columns on a narrow screen.
Use the menu if dragging feels awkward.

sections.title: Read the indicators
paragraphs: <label>Overview</label> counts projects, total tasks, open tasks, completed tasks, overdue tasks and completion rate. Open means not <status value="done">Done</status>. Overdue means unfinished with a due date before today, using local dates. Project progress is the proportion currently <status value="done">Done</status>, not hours or effort.

sections.title: Interpret the charts
paragraphs: <label>Status</label> and priority distributions describe tasks still here. <label>Created and completed</label> compares the last 14 local days using retained creation and current completion dates. Reopening or deleting can remove an earlier completion: this is not an immutable activity log. <action>View daily counts</action> opens a readable table.

sections.title: Turn an insight into action
paragraphs: Linked indicators, statuses and priorities open <label>My Tasks</label> with the corresponding filter. <label>Tasks to watch</label> groups upcoming deadlines, overdue tasks and recent updates. Project progress links open projects. Saturnino does not calculate time tracking, team velocity or forecasts.

customization.title: Customization
customization.intro: Make the workspace fit your way of working.

sections.title: Theme and language
steps: Use the header or <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Appearance and language</label></path> to select <label>Light</label> or <label>Dark</label> and <label>English</label> or <label>Português</label>.
Changes apply immediately and are saved in this browser when storage is available.
Dates, forms and this guide follow the selected language.

sections.title: Arrange your sidebar
steps: Choose <action>Customize sidebar</action> in the sidebar or <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Sidebar</label></path>.
Toggle sections and move them using the available controls.
<action>Save changes</action> applies the draft; <action>Cancel</action> or <key>Escape</key> discards it.
<action>Reset sidebar preferences</action> prepares defaults in the draft: save to apply.
<label>Favorites</label> belong to projects and recent projects follow your visits.

sections.title: Compact mode and width
steps: On desktop, resize with the sidebar divider or choose a width in <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Sidebar</label></path>.
Use <label>Compact sidebar</label> to reduce its footprint; turn it off for the full layout.
Small screens use a navigation drawer.
These preferences are separate from a JSON workspace backup.

productivity.title: Make the most of Saturnino
productivity.intro: Small habits make your workspace useful.

sections.title: Start with a manageable goal
bullets: Separate work, study and personal goals into projects.
Break big goals into small tasks: <example>Create wireframes</example> is clearer than <example>Finish the website</example>.
Keep future ideas in <status value="backlog">Backlog</status> and choose realistic priorities and dates.

sections.title: Keep the next step visible
bullets: Limit how much work is <status value="in-progress">In progress</status> at once.
Favorite frequent projects and review <label>Overview</label> regularly.
Customize the sidebar, choose a comfortable theme and install the app if supported.

sections.title: Build a backup habit
paragraphs: Save JSON backups regularly, especially before clearing browser data, moving devices or restoring another file. Keep copies somewhere you can find again. CSV helps review tasks externally but cannot restore a workspace.

local-first.title: Local-first & Privacy
local-first.intro: Your workspace lives in this browser and device.

sections.title: What stays local
paragraphs: No account is required. Projects, tasks and favorites are stored in the browser's local database. Theme, language and sidebar preferences are stored separately. Installing as a PWA does not add cloud backup or synchronization.

sections.title: Each environment is independent
paragraphs: Computer, tablet and phone each have a separate workspace. Other browsers, profiles or site addresses can have different storage on the same device. Transfer work explicitly with a JSON export and restore. A redirect does not transfer local data.

sections.title: Protect your device and files
paragraphs: Clearing site data, private sessions, device failure or browser storage eviction can make records unavailable. This architecture does not encrypt local records or protect them from someone with access to your browser profile. Keep backups. Hosting and external links may make network requests; local-first is not an absolute privacy guarantee.

offline.title: Offline Usage
offline.intro: Keep working once the app is ready on your device.

sections.title: Prepare before disconnecting
steps: Open Saturnino online and allow application files to finish loading.
<path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Local Workspace</label></path>: wait for <label>Ready for offline use.</label> Installation alone does not prove the cache is complete.

sections.title: What works offline
paragraphs: With cache ready and local storage available, create/edit projects and tasks, move cards, filter and review progress. This guide and its bundled images are cached with the app; external references need Internet. Storage limits and eviction still apply. Offline is not synchronization or backup.

sections.title: Update after saving
steps: When online, use <action>Check for updates</action> in <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Local Workspace</label></path>.
Save your work before <action>Reload to update</action>.
Unsaved forms may ask to continue editing or discard.
Saved records remain local, but an update does not create a backup.
Do not clear site data just to update.

backup.title: Backup & Restore
backup.intro: A saved file lets you recover or move your workspace.

sections.title: Download a JSON backup
steps: Open <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Data management</label></path>.
Choose <action>Download JSON backup</action> and locate the .json file.
Keep it somewhere you control, ideally off the device too. Protect files containing sensitive information.

sections.title: Preview before replacing
steps: Export the destination's existing workspace first if there is anything to keep.
Choose <action>Restore JSON backup</action>, select the file and review its name, date and current/selected project and task counts.
Choose <action>Replace workspace</action> only if you accept replacing ALL local projects and tasks. Records absent from the file are removed. <action>Cancel</action> leaves data unchanged.
Check expected projects, tasks, favorites, dates and order after restoring. To transfer devices, move the JSON file yourself and repeat at the destination.
sections.warning: <action>Replace workspace</action> replaces all local projects and tasks. Records absent from the selected backup are removed. Export the current workspace before continuing.

sections.title: What JSON and CSV contain
paragraphs: JSON includes projects (color and favorites) and tasks (planning fields, status, order and timestamps). It excludes theme, language, sidebar layout/width/compact mode, recent history and app cache. Restore accepts a validated Saturnino JSON backup up to 20 MiB. <action>Export tasks as CSV</action> makes a table for spreadsheets or external review; CSV cannot restore a workspace. Restore replaces, it does not merge or synchronize.
sections.note: JSON is the recovery format. CSV is for external analysis and cannot restore your workspace.

limitations.title: Current Limitations
limitations.intro: Know what is available before relying on it.

sections.title: Not available today
bullets: No cloud storage or automatic cross-device synchronization.
No team collaboration or shared workspace.

sections.title: Local storage needs care
paragraphs: Clearing storage can remove your work. Private profiles, another browser or device may open an empty workspace. There is no trash or automatic recovery service. A new installation cannot recover lost local records: keep JSON backups.

sections.title: Browser differences
paragraphs: Installation options and programmatic prompts vary by platform. Offline needs a completed initial cache and available storage. External links require Internet. Use menus instead of drag and drop when a gesture is uncomfortable.

future.title: Future Vision
future.intro: An optional connected workspace, with a local-first foundation.

sections.title: A direction, not a release promise
paragraphs: The long-term vision includes optional accounts, authentication and cloud synchronization for the same workspace across devices. Preserving local work and offline access is part of that vision. These features are NOT implemented in this version and have no promised date.

sections.title: Today and a possible tomorrow
paragraphs: Today, each browser profile and origin holds independent records; transfer uses JSON files. A future optional service would connect devices through an authenticated account while retaining local use. Migration, permissions and conflict handling would need careful implementation first.

sections.title: Useful today
paragraphs: Organize projects, plan tasks, use Kanban and keep backups now, without waiting for cloud features. This guide only teaches features you can use today.

faq.question: Is Saturnino free?
faq.answer: The currently published application can be used without payment or an account. This is not a promise about the terms of future optional services.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: No. The current workspace is local-first and has no sign-in.

faq.question: Where are my projects stored?
faq.answer: In this browser profile's local database for this site address. A JSON file you export is a separate copy.

faq.question: Can I work without Internet?
faq.answer: Yes, after an online visit finishes caching and <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Local Workspace</label></path> reports <label>Ready for offline use.</label> External links still need a connection.

faq.question: How do I install on a computer?
faq.answer: Use the installation chapter: Chrome's install menu, Edge's <label>App available</label> icon, or Safari <label>Add to Dock</label> on compatible Macs.

faq.question: How do I install on iPhone or iPad?
faq.answer: Open the site in Safari, <path><label>Share</label> → <label>Add to Home Screen</label></path>. Enable <label>Open as Web App</label> when offered, then <label>Add</label>. Menu names vary by system version.

faq.question: Why is there no install button?
faq.answer: The browser may not support a programmatic prompt, may not consider it ready, or the app may already be installed. Use manual instructions or continue in a tab.

faq.question: Can I use the same projects on several devices?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Export JSON from the source and restore at the destination. There is no merge or cloud sync.

faq.question: How do I make a backup?
faq.answer: <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Data management</label> → <action>Download JSON backup</action></path>. Find and keep the file in a safe location.

faq.question: How do I restore my data?
faq.answer: Back up current data first. Choose <action>Restore JSON backup</action>, review counts and confirm <action>Replace workspace</action> only when ready. CSV is not a restore file.

faq.question: What if I clear browser data?
faq.answer: <label>Projects</label> and tasks may be removed. You will need an existing JSON backup to recover supported data; the app cannot reconstruct deleted local records.

faq.question: Why are projects missing in another browser?
faq.answer: Browsers, profiles, devices and origins use separate storage. Return to the original environment or restore a backup; do not clear it.

faq.question: How do I update the app?
faq.answer: Online, <path><label>Settings</label> → <label>Local Workspace</label> → <action>Check for updates</action></path>. Save edits, then <action>Reload to update</action> when offered.

faq.question: What if a task does not appear?
faq.answer: Clear search and filters, check its project and status column, and check the browser profile/address. Reopen the page if loading failed. Do not restore over your workspace until you have backed it up and reviewed the replacement preview.

platforms.title: macOS · Safari or Chrome
steps: In Safari on a compatible macOS version, open Saturnino, then <path><label>Share</label> → <label>Add to Dock</label></path> (or <path><label>File</label> → <label>Add to Dock</label></path>). Confirm the name and <label>Add</label>.
In Chrome, use the address-bar install icon when offered, or <path><label>More</label> → <label>Cast, save, and share</label> → <label>Install page as app</label></path>. Follow the browser dialog.
Open it from the Dock or app launcher. Check the workspace before relying on existing records.

platforms.title: Windows · Edge or Chrome
steps: In Edge, open Saturnino and choose the <label>App available</label> icon in the address bar when offered, then <label>Install</label>.
In Chrome, choose the install icon or <path><label>More</label> → <label>Cast, save, and share</label> → <label>Install page as app</label></path>.
Follow the browser prompt, then open Saturnino from your app launcher.

platforms.title: iPhone · Safari
steps: Open Saturnino in Safari, then tap <label>Share</label> (use <label>More</label> or <label>View More</label> if your system places it there).
Choose <label>Add to Home Screen</label>. Enable <label>Open as Web App</label> when available.
Confirm <label>Add</label>, then open Saturnino from the Home Screen. No App Store download is needed.

platforms.title: iPad · Safari
steps: Open Saturnino in Safari and choose <label>Share</label> (then <label>More</label> or <label>View More</label> if needed).
Choose <label>Add to Home Screen</label> and enable <label>Open as Web App</label> when offered.
Tap <label>Add</label> and open the icon from the Home Screen. Check your local workspace.

platforms.title: Android · Chrome
steps: Open Saturnino in Chrome and open <label>More</label> beside the address bar.
Choose <path><label>Install and create shortcut</label> → <label>Install</label></path>, or <label>Install app</label>/<label>Add to Home screen</label> if your browser uses that label.
Follow the prompt and launch the icon. No Google Play download is needed.
